comment: Prebuilt, vendored Basis Universal codec modules. NEVER edit these artifacts; re-vendor from the pinned upstreams and update the hashes here.

basis_transcoder.js.version: basis_universal master @ 073eb6a0a34a23d77e75e54f41dcd9653a52da83 (2026-10-30; no release tag contains NO_DYNAMIC_EXECUTION yet) + basisu-trim.patch, built locally with Emscripten 6.0.10 (emsdk 708dcbcc9ee23bc7d2dad44fc90db377e38b771c). Eval-free embind glue (DYNAMIC_EXECUTION=0 + EMBIND_AOT=1): no eval()/new Function(), loads under a CSP with 'wasm-unsafe-eval' and without 'unsafe-eval'. KTX2+Zstd, non-pthread, MODULARIZE+UMD, EXPORT_NAME=BASIS. Byte-identical to the previous (untrimmed) build's .js: the format trim only changes the .wasm.
basis_transcoder.js.build: git apply basisu-trim.patch && emcmake cmake -S webgl/transcoder -B build -G "Unix Makefiles" -DNO_DYNAMIC_EXECUTION=ON "-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-sINITIAL_MEMORY=16MB -sMAXIMUM_MEMORY=256MB" "-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-UBASISD_SUPPORT_ETC2_EAC_RG11 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_ETC2_EAC_RG11=1 -UBASISD_SUPPORT_UASTC_HDR -DBASISD_SUPPORT_UASTC_HDR=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_XUASTC=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_PVRTC1=0" && cmake --build build
basis_transcoder.js.link_command: em++ -sINITIAL_MEMORY=16MB -sMAXIMUM_MEMORY=256MB --bind -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 -O3 -s MALLOC=emmalloc -s MODULARIZE=1 -s EXPORT_NAME=BASIS -s ASSERTIONS=0 -s EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS=['HEAP8'] -s DYNAMIC_EXECUTION=0 -s EMBIND_AOT=1 <objs> -o basis_transcoder.js
basis_transcoder.js.compile_flags: -std=gnu++17 -O3 -fno-strict-aliasing -DNDEBUG -DBASISD_SUPPORT_KTX2=1 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_KTX2_ZSTD=1 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_UASTC=1 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_UASTC_HDR=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_XUASTC=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_PVRTC1=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_BC7=1 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_ETC2_EAC_RG11=1 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_ATC=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_PVRTC2=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_FXT1=0 -DBASISD_SUPPORT_ASTC_HIGHER_OPAQUE_QUALITY=0 -DBASISU_SUPPORT_ENCODING=0 -DBASISD_ENABLE_DEBUG_FLAGS=1 (upstream CMakeLists defaults except ETC2_EAC_RG11=1, UASTC_HDR=0, XUASTC=0, PVRTC1=0, all set from the command line in CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS)
basis_transcoder.js.rebuild: rebuild-transcoder.sh <work-dir> beside this file (pins both commits, applies basisu-trim.patch beside it, installs emsdk inside <work-dir>, verifies the patch and both artifact sha256s)
basis_transcoder.js.license: LICENSE-basis_universal (Apache-2.0); statically links Zstd (LICENSE-zstd-BSD-3-clause.txt, BSD-3-Clause; Zstd is dual BSD/GPLv2, BSD chosen)

basis_transcoder.wasm.version: basis_universal master @ 073eb6a0a34a23d77e75e54f41dcd9653a52da83 + basisu-trim.patch, Emscripten 6.0.10. 552,629 bytes (209,607 brotli-11 / 251,961 gzip-9); the untrimmed build was 1,061,651 (360,650 / 451,098) and three.js r185's v1.50 was 527,333 (203,605 / 244,575). Memory: initial 256 pages (16 MiB), maximum 4096 pages (256 MiB). Formats compiled in: sources ETC1S and UASTC LDR 4x4 (KTX2, BasisLZ / Zstd / none), every LDR target incl. ETC2 EAC RG11; compiled out: UASTC HDR 4x4, ASTC HDR 6x6, UASTC HDR 6x6, XUASTC LDR, ASTC LDR and XUBC7 sources, the HDR targets and PVRTC1. Output for every ETC1S / UASTC LDR source x the 9 worker targets is byte-identical to the untrimmed build (sha256 751a007d46cd295f1aed9bffe593aaf8fbca3b3622aeef5892253845f61ef7fc).

basis_encoder.js.version: basis_universal v2_1_0r (official prebuilt web encoder, non-pthread single-thread build)

basisu-trim.patch.upstream: local patch to basis_universal 073eb6a0 transcoder/basisu_transcoder.cpp (+18/-4 lines), applied by rebuild-transcoder.sh
basisu-trim.patch.version: Adds the #if guards upstream's own BASISD_SUPPORT_UASTC_HDR / BASISD_SUPPORT_XUASTC switches need to compile when turned off (at this commit, either switch set to 0 fails to compile). Guards only: with upstream's default defines the patched source builds a .wasm byte-identical to the unpatched one. Drop it once upstream fixes the switches.

notes: Non-pthread builds only — no SharedArrayBuffer, no COOP/COEP headers required.

Both JS files are Emscripten MODULARIZE+UMD builds and BOTH export the SAME global factory name `BASIS`. Never load both into one scope naively; capture-and-delete the global between loads, or host them in separate workers.

Transcoder: eval-free build (no 'unsafe-eval' needed; 'wasm-unsafe-eval' still is). It replaces the three.js r185 copy, which was byte-identical to basis_universal v1_50_0's prebuilt (2024-09-10) and used new Function() in embind. The ENCODER (v2_1_0r prebuilt) still uses new Function(): an app that ships it cannot drop 'unsafe-eval'.
The transcoder (master @ 073eb6a, 2026-10-30) is now newer than the encoder (v2_1_0r). ETC1S / UASTC-LDR bitstreams are stable across these versions.

Pair this transcoder with web/workers/basis-worker.js as it is in this repo (sha256 338e3b2a0c474d28d86010434b921e2434428a67df1a00b0f8b72814fb2b3b6d). For ETC1S -> BC7 only, the worker calls transcodeImageWithFlags(..., cDecodeFlagsNoETC1SChromaFiltering=64, ...), so output stays byte-identical to the v1.50/r185 transcoder and as fast; it also reloads the module after a wasm abort. It feature-detects, so it still works with the old transcoder. With an older worker, ETC1S -> BC7 gets v2's chroma filtering: different bytes, 2-5x slower on that path.

Transcoder max memory is 256 MiB (was 2 GiB). Measured worst case for 4096x4096 (UASTC+Zstd -> RGBA32 fallback) is 115 MiB, 131 MiB after a session of back-to-back 4096 textures. Over the cap, a transcode fails cleanly (transcodeImage returns false -> worker 'transcode-failed'); the module stays usable. First thing that fails: RGBA32 output at 8192x8192 (needs ~278 MiB).

ETC1S -> EAC RG11 works since the 0.40.1 build (BASISD_SUPPORT_ETC2_EAC_RG11=1). The renderer picks EAC RG11 for two-channel-packed normal maps on ETC2-only GPUs (most phones); with upstream's default build every such ETC1S transcode failed (cleanly, in under 1 ms: the scene loader logged it and left the normal slot unbound, so the surface rendered flat). UASTC -> EAC RG11 worked before and is unchanged. Verified on 14 files x 9 targets: the 9 ETC1S -> EAC RG11 combinations go from failing to succeeding, the other 117 are byte-identical to the previous build, and a packed normal map decoded from the EAC RG11 output matches its source at 43.5 dB (BC5 from the same file: 43.3 dB).

Rebuilding: use Emscripten 3.1.51..7.0.0. On 7.0.1+ EMBIND_AOT changes meaning (ES-module exports); upstream's NO_DYNAMIC_EXECUTION option still adds -sEMBIND_AOT=1 unconditionally, so re-check before bumping.

rebuild-transcoder.sh beside this file reproduces both transcoder artifacts byte-for-byte (pins basis_universal + emsdk, installs emsdk inside its work dir). Its own comments call the output directory dist/ — that is where it was developed; here the artifacts live beside it.
Encoder ships to the EDITOR only. Player apps copy the transcoder pair only.
LICENSE-three.js is kept for history; no artifact here comes from three.js any more.

Transcoder format trim (0.40.x follow-up): the renderer only sends the worker KTX2 files with vkFormat 0 (codec-basis selection.rs sniff_basis_ktx2) and only asks for the 9 LDR targets in basis-worker.js TARGET_TO_ENUM; the editor encodes only ETC1S or UASTC LDR 4x4 (setUASTC). So the transcoder is built without UASTC HDR, XUASTC LDR, ASTC LDR, XUBC7 and PVRTC1 support: .wasm 1,061,651 -> 552,629 bytes (brotli 360,650 -> 209,607). Verified in Chrome 157 through the real worker under the strict CSP: 126/126 file x target outputs of the 14-file bench byte-identical, plus UASTC without Zstd, non-multiple-of-4 and linear files; HDR sources fail on every LDR target with or without the trim. What changes: a XUASTC LDR KTX2 (vkFormat 0, supercompression 5, DFD model 169; not allowed by KHR_texture_basisu, never written by our pipeline) used to transcode and now fails cleanly ('transcode-failed', module stays usable), as it did with the r185 transcoder. The embind surface is unchanged (same exports, methods and enum values).

Since 0.40.1 codec-basis selection.rs sniff_basis_ktx2 also refuses a vkFormat-0 KTX2 whose supercompression scheme is not 0 (none), 1 (BasisLZ) or 2 (Zstandard), so a XUASTC LDR file (scheme 5) or any later scheme is turned away before it reaches the worker, with the same 'not a Basis KTX2 this build can transcode' error a native KTX2 gets.
